opening.argument: The video is presented as a Hindi discussion about fear, death, grief, and emotional dependence, framed as reflective guidance rather than a deceptive transaction. It explains that “The problem is not death. The problem is what we think about death,” then offers a 21-day affirmation practice and asks participants to email the team about changes they observe. Those instructions invite personal reflection without guaranteeing results. The closing invitation to subscribe and register for a live session for free is ordinary audience engagement and event promotion. Nothing described requires payment, solicits an investment, requests credentials, or establishes a deceptive transaction; the speaker also states, “I'm not selling your information, all I'm asking is why don't you listen.”

citations.quote: the problem is not death. The problem is what we think about death
For the next 21 days I'm showing you one task. Okay. Daily, morning and night you have to listen to my morning and night affirmations.
After 21 days we need an e-mail to our team telling them about the changes that are on your mind.
I'm not selling your information, all I'm asking is why don't you listen.
